# Swedish Literature — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/swedish-literature.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/swedish-literature.ttl`](../decks/swedish-literature.ttl) · **Cards:** 60 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

60 works of Swedish literature and their authors, from Bellman's Fredman's Epistles (Fredmans epistlar, 1790) to the crime novels and bestsellers of the 21st century: novels, plays, poetry and children's books written in Swedish by Swedish authors. The works were chosen by how widely Wikimedia sites cover them and how often they have been published in Sweden (records in LIBRIS), at most three per author. Front: the title in Swedish and in English (the Swedish title for the four works with no English edition found); back: the author. Compiled from Wikidata and LIBRIS, the National Library of Sweden's catalogue, and checked against Wikipedia and Open Library.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0 1.0. Its content sources are CC0: Wikidata (the candidate works, sitelinks, Swedish titles, English labels and aliases, authors and their names) and LIBRIS (record counts for the ranking, and the titles of English editions, which are bibliographic facts; KB releases the Swedish national bibliography under CC0; from records outside it, such as editions published abroad, the deck takes only bibliographic facts (that an edition with a given title by a given author exists, and how many records there are), which copyright does not protect, and it consulted only a small number of single records, not a substantial part of the database). Open Library (no licence stated), Litteraturbanken (no licence for its catalogue data found) and the Swedish and English Wikipedias (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed authors and English editions; no wording and no selection was taken from them. The English Wikipedia article title is used only to choose among English titles that LIBRIS or Open Library show were published, so the title on the card is a fact about an edition, not text taken from Wikipedia; this decided two cards, Gösta Berling's Saga and The Stonecutter, whose English titles are attested by LIBRIS but are not Wikidata English names. The selection is the result of the ranking rule applied to Wikidata and LIBRIS data, not a list copied from any source.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. 1. Candidates (Wikidata, 2026-10-04). Four queries were combined: query 1 (<scratch>/pool2.py) takes every item in Swedish (P407 Q9027) or from Sweden (P495 Q34) whose author (P50) is a Swedish citizen (P27 Q34) and that at least 2 Wikimedia sites cover (wikibase:sitelinks ≥ 2): 722 items. Query 2 lists the Swedish citizens whose occupation (P106) is writer, novelist, poet, playwright or children's writer with at least 15 sitelinks (310 people) and query 3 every item they are the author of (7,400 items, of which those with ≥ 2 sitelinks were kept), which adds works without a language statement. Query 4 adds works whose author is a group (not a human) whose members (P527) are Swedish citizens: for some of the Martin Beck novels the query service lists only the partnership Sjöwall and Wahlöö (Q2342834) as author, and Hypnotisören has the pen name Lars Kepler (Q1806270). Together: 853 items.
3. 2. Eligibility (script eligible.py). Dropped: 71 items whose type (P31) is not a single book (film, television, series of books or comics, songs, hymns and single poems, documents, manifestos, maps, scholarly articles and the like); 67 with a language statement that is not Swedish (Latin, English, German, French, Finnish …: Linnaeus's botanical works, Swedenborg, Munthe's The Story of San Michele, Peter Weiss's German plays, Strindberg's Inferno and En dåres försvarstal, written in French); 23 without a Swedish label; and 3 edition items duplicating a work (same Swedish label and authors). 689 works remained.
4. 3. LIBRIS count (script libris_count.py). For each of the 689 works, LIBRIS was searched with the xsearch API, tit:"<Swedish title>" förf:<author's surname> (the Swedish label without a parenthesised disambiguator such as "(roman)"; the surname is the last word of the author's Swedish, mul or English label; for the two groups Sjöwall and Kepler), reading every result page of 200. A record counts when its language is Swedish ("swe"), its creator contains the surname and its title is the work's title alone or followed by a subtitle or statement (" :", " /", " ;", ",", "."), case-insensitively. The count measures how often the work has been published and catalogued in Sweden (printed editions, reprints, e-books, audiobooks and talking books).
5. 4. Ranking (script rank.py). Each work's score is the geometric mean of its sitelinks and its LIBRIS count, √(sitelinks × records). Sitelinks measure how widely the work is known abroad; the LIBRIS count how much it has been published at home. Either alone gave a skewed list (see Quality control): sitelinks favour recent international bestsellers and give some classics few (Röda rummet and Hemsöborna have 8 sitelinks each, Utvandrarna 3), while LIBRIS counts favour nineteenth- and early twentieth-century works with many reprints. Works were taken in order of score, at most three per author (an author partnership counts as one author), until 60 were chosen; the 60th has score 9.2 (Jack: √(17 × 5)) and the next eligible work 9.1, so the cut falls between two values. Ties are broken by the LIBRIS count, then by item id.
6. 5. Hand exclusions. Every work ranked above the cut was read for whether it is a work of fiction, poetry or drama written in Swedish. Three were excluded (see Selection): Olaus Magnus's Historia om de nordiska folken (a Latin work of history, in Swedish translation), Viktor Rydberg's Tomten (a single poem) and Lennart Nilsson's Ett barn blir till (photographic non-fiction).
7. 6. Swedish titles. The Swedish front is the work's Wikidata Swedish label, which on every card is also the title of the earliest dated Swedish-language LIBRIS record of the work (for Gösta Berlings saga a facsimile of the 1890 competition manuscript; the first edition is from 1891) (followed by a subtitle on some, e.g. "Röda rummet : skildringar ur artist- och författarlifvet", 1879). Singoalla's label is "Singoalla (roman)", with a disambiguator; the card uses "Singoalla", the title in LIBRIS.
8. 7. English titles (script resolve.py, corrected by hand in quality-control rounds 1–2). Candidates, in order: the English Wikipedia article title (without a parenthesised disambiguator), the Wikidata English label and the Wikidata English aliases. A candidate is attested when LIBRIS has an English-language record, or Open Library an English-language work, by the author whose title is the candidate alone or with a subtitle, compared case- and accent-insensitively. The first attested candidate is the English front. Six fronts were then set by hand: "Frithiof's Saga" and "The Markurells of Wadköping" (English editions from 1833 and 2016 whose titles differ from Wikidata's English names only by an apostrophe or a leading article, which the comparison did not ignore); "Sara Videbeck" (the title of the English translation of Det går an, 1919, which had no candidate); "Fredman's Epistles" and "Fredman's Songs" (the Wikidata English labels and the names English Wikipedia gives; the two collections were published in English together as "Fredman's Epistles & Songs", 1977–1999); and "Ronia, the Robber's Daughter" (the title of the English editions of 1983, 1985 and 2010, a Wikidata English alias and the name in the English Wikipedia lead, rather than the "Ronja" spelling of one 2018 edition and of the article title). Nine cards show the Swedish title on the English side: five because their English editions keep it (Kallocain 1966, Singoalla 1903, Aniara 1963, Roseanna 1967, Barabbas 1951: LIBRIS English-language records and Open Library works, on each card), four because no English edition was found in LIBRIS or Open Library (Ondskan, Kattresan, Svinalängorna, Jack). The English title is a fact about a published edition; on every card with an English title it is backed by a LIBRIS record, an Open Library work or both (see each card's evidence), except Fredman's Epistles and Fredman's Songs: their English names are the Wikidata English labels, and the texts were published in English only together, as Fredman's Epistles & Songs (LIBRIS also has Peter Dahl's lithographs, "Fredman's epistles : lithographs", 1984). The four Swedish-only fronts have no English edition.
9. 8. Authors. The back is the author's Wikidata English and Swedish label (or mul label where a language has none: August Strindberg and Hjalmar Söderberg have no English label, Esaias Tegnér no Swedish label); all are written the same in both languages. The four Martin Beck novels' author is the partnership Sjöwall and Wahlöö (Q2342834, P527 Maj Sjöwall Q264855 and Per Wahlöö Q553730); the back names both people, "Maj Sjöwall and Per Wahlöö" / "Maj Sjöwall och Per Wahlöö", as LIBRIS and the Wikipedia leads do. Hypnotisören's author is the pen name Lars Kepler (Q1806270), which is the name on the book; a note names the two writers behind it (P527).
10. 9. Cross-checks. For every card with a Swedish Wikipedia article (59 works; Det som inte dödar oss has none) its lead and, where there is one (56 works), the English Wikipedia article linked from Wikidata was fetched with the MediaWiki API; a script checked that each lead contains the author's surname (all do). The LIBRIS Swedish records confirm title and author (the creator heading of each counted record contains the surname). The evidence on every card was generated by make_cards.py from the saved responses, not typed by hand; the scripts are not published, their rules are the ones above, and Selection lists the works just below the cut and those left out by the per-author cap with their scores.
11. 10. Machine checks: 371 Wikidata checks run by the builder against live Wikidata: on every card the author (P50; the group item for the partnerships), the language Swedish (P407 Q9027), the Swedish title as sv label (all but Singoalla), the English-side front as en label or alias where it is one (54 cards: the title of the English edition, the English name of Bellman's two collections, and on Kattresan, Svinalängorna and Jack the Swedish title, which is also their en label; the en label checks on Kallocain, Singoalla, Aniara, Roseanna and Barabbas were added in quality-control round 4, those on Kattresan, Svinalängorna and Jack in round 5; Ondskan is not checked, as its en label 'Evil' is not on the card), and the author's English and Swedish labels (for the partnerships, P527 of the group item and the members' labels). The built deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (validate_sources.ts).
12. 11. Earlier attempts, recorded for completeness. A first candidate query on Swedish-language works only (q1) missed works without a P407 statement; queries starting from all works by Swedish citizens timed out (502/timeout) and were replaced by queries 1–4. A ranking by sitelinks alone (with three or four works per author) was tried and rejected for the reasons in step 4; Wikidata's notable work (P800) of Swedish writers was looked at and found too patchy to select from. Litteraturbanken was probed as a further check of the older works: its rights page (https://litteraturbanken.se/om/rattigheter) is a JavaScript application whose text neither curl nor WebFetch returned, two web searches ("Litteraturbanken rättigheter texter fri användning licens", "litteraturbanken.se om rättigheter upphovsrätt texterna") found no licence statement for its data, and the first lookup in its public API (query 18, <scratch>/lb.py) reported only 4 of the 60 works (Röda rummet, Singoalla, Det går an, Frithiofs saga). That count was wrong: the script matched authors on a field (work_authors) that most records do not have. Rerun in quality-control round 3 on the field the records do have (authors; <scratch>/lb2.py), the same API finds 20 of the 60 works by the card's author under the card's Swedish title: Nils Holgerssons underbara resa genom Sverige, Gösta Berlings saga, Fröken Julie, Kallocain, Hemsöborna, Röde Orm, Röda rummet, Singoalla, Herr Arnes penningar, Doktor Glas, Aniara, Fredmans epistlar, Den allvarsamma leken, Det går an, Frithiofs saga, Martin Bircks ungdom, Markurells i Wadköping, Fredmans sånger, Bränt barn and Kattresan. Each record carries its own licence field ("pd", "cc-0" and Litteraturbanken's own licences, e.g. "lb-svs"). Litteraturbanken holds mainly older texts, so it covers a third of the deck; it serves as a verification source for those 20 works and was not used to select or word anything.

## Selection

The deck holds the 60 highest-scoring works of fiction, poetry, drama and children's literature written in Swedish by Swedish authors, as of 2026-10-04, with at most three works per author. Eligible works are those that Wikidata gives a Swedish author (a Swedish citizen, or a partnership of Swedish citizens) and that are in Swedish or from Sweden, covered by at least two Wikimedia sites; the score is the geometric mean of the work's Wikimedia sitelinks and its number of Swedish-language LIBRIS records. Left out by rule: book series and series items (the Millennium trilogy as a whole, Utvandrarserien, Barnen i Bullerbyn, Pettson och Findus; the individual novels compete instead), films, songs, hymns and single poems, and works not written in Swedish (Strindberg's Inferno and En dåres försvarstal were written in French; Linnaeus and Swedenborg wrote in Latin); Finland-Swedish literature is not in the pool because its authors are not Swedish citizens in Wikidata (query 20: Johan Ludvig Runeberg, Edith Södergran and Tove Jansson are citizens of Finland, the Grand Duchy of Finland or the Russian Empire). Left out by hand, although they ranked high enough: Historia om de nordiska folken by Olaus Magnus (written in Latin, 1555; history, not literature), Tomten by Viktor Rydberg (a single poem) and Ett barn blir till by Lennart Nilsson (photographic non-fiction). The cap of three per author left out, among others, Strindberg's Fadren, Ett drömspel and Mäster Olof, Selma Lagerlöf's Jerusalem, Kejsarn av Portugallien and Körkarlen, Astrid Lindgren's Mio, min Mio and Mästerdetektiven Blomkvist, and further novels by Henning Mankell and by Sjöwall and Wahlöö. Sitelink and LIBRIS counts change over time; the ranking is a snapshot of 2026-10-04 and decides only which works are in the deck. Around the cut (score √(sitelinks × LIBRIS records), 2026-10-04): the 58th to 60th works are Strändernas svall 9.4, Barn av sin stad 9.3 and Jack 9.2; Ett barn blir till (9.2) was excluded by hand, Strindberg's Ensam (9.2) and Läckberg's Olycksfågeln (9.2) by the cap; the next eligible works are Hjalmar Bergman's Hans nåds testamente 9.1, Elin Wägner's Pennskaftet 9.0, Per Anders Fogelström's Mina drömmars stad 8.8, Annika Thor's En ö i havet 8.7 and Karin Alvtegen's Skam 8.7. Highest-scoring works left out by the cap: Mio, min Mio 28.1, Fadren 27.1, Ett drömspel 25.7, Jerusalem 23.9, Kejsarn av Portugallien 21.9, Mäster Olof 21.5, Körkarlen 19.5, Mästerdetektiven Blomkvist 17.9, En herrgårdssägen 17.2, Löwensköldska ringen 17.1, Dödsdansen 16.0, Mannen på balkongen (Sjöwall and Wahlöö) 15.6, Den vedervärdige mannen från Säffle 14.5 and Hundarna i Riga (Mankell) 14.5.

## Queries

**1. Candidate pool: works in Swedish or from Sweden whose author is a Swedish citizen, at least 2 sitelinks (run by <scratch>/pool2.py, POST to https://query.wikidata.org/sparql; result <scratch>/pool2.json, details per item with query 5)** (Wikidata: literary works with a Swedish author, their labels, authors (P50), language (P407) and sitelinks)

```
SELECT DISTINCT ?item ?sitelinks WHERE {
  { ?item wdt:P407 wd:Q9027 . } UNION { ?item wdt:P495 wd:Q34 . }
  ?item wdt:P50 ?author ; wikibase:sitelinks ?sitelinks .
  FILTER(?sitelinks >= 2)
  ?author wdt:P27 wd:Q34 .
}

```

**2. Swedish writers (occupation writer, novelist, poet, playwright, children's writer) with at least 15 sitelinks (run by <scratch>/authors.py)** (Wikidata: literary works with a Swedish author, their labels, authors (P50), language (P407) and sitelinks)

```
SELECT ?author ?sitelinks (SAMPLE(?en) AS ?enLabel) (SAMPLE(?sv) AS ?svLabel) (SAMPLE(?mul) AS ?mulLabel) WHERE {
  VALUES ?occ { wd:Q36180 wd:Q6625963 wd:Q49757 wd:Q214917 wd:Q4853732 }
  ?author wdt:P27 wd:Q34 ; wdt:P106 ?occ ; wikibase:sitelinks ?sitelinks .
  FILTER(?sitelinks >= 15)
  OPTIONAL { ?author rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?author rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?author rdfs:label ?mul FILTER(LANG(?mul) = "mul") }
} GROUP BY ?author ?sitelinks

```

**3. Every work by those writers, 25 authors per request (%s = their ids; run by <scratch>/authors.py)** (Wikidata: literary works with a Swedish author, their labels, authors (P50), language (P407) and sitelinks)

```
SELECT ?item ?sitelinks (SAMPLE(?sv) AS ?svLabel) (SAMPLE(?en) AS ?enLabel)
  (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?a), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?authors)
  (MIN(YEAR(?date)) AS ?firstYear)
  (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?type), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?types)
  (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?typeEn; separator="|") AS ?typeNames)
  (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?lang), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?langs) WHERE {
  VALUES ?author { %s }
  ?item wdt:P50 ?author ; wikibase:sitelinks ?sitelinks .
  ?item wdt:P50 ?a .
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P31 ?type . OPTIONAL { ?type rdfs:label ?typeEn FILTER(LANG(?typeEn) = "en") } }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P407 ?lang . }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P577 ?date . }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv . FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?en . FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
} GROUP BY ?item ?sitelinks

```

**4. Works whose author is a group of Swedish citizens (sh <scratch>/run.sh q6b)** (Wikidata: literary works with a Swedish author, their labels, authors (P50), language (P407) and sitelinks)

```
SELECT ?item ?sitelinks (SAMPLE(?sv) AS ?svLabel) (SAMPLE(?en) AS ?enLabel) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?group), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?authors) (MIN(YEAR(?date)) AS ?firstYear) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?typeEn; separator="|") AS ?typeNames) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?lang), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?langs) WHERE {
  ?group wdt:P527 ?member .
  ?member wdt:P27 wd:Q34 ; wdt:P31 wd:Q5 .
  ?item wdt:P50 ?group ; wikibase:sitelinks ?sitelinks .
  FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?group wdt:P31 wd:Q5 }
  FILTER(?sitelinks >= 2)
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P31 ?type . OPTIONAL { ?type rdfs:label ?typeEn FILTER(LANG(?typeEn) = "en") } }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P407 ?lang . }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P577 ?date . }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv . FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?en . FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
}
GROUP BY ?item ?sitelinks
ORDER BY DESC(?sitelinks)

```

**5. Labels, authors, type, language and year of the pool items, 200 per request (%s = item ids)** (Wikidata: literary works with a Swedish author, their labels, authors (P50), language (P407) and sitelinks)

```
SELECT ?item (SAMPLE(?sv) AS ?svLabel) (SAMPLE(?en) AS ?enLabel)
  (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?author), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?authors)
  (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?authorEn; separator="|") AS ?authorNames)
  (MIN(YEAR(?date)) AS ?firstYear)
  (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?type), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?types)
  (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?typeEn; separator="|") AS ?typeNames)
  (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?lang), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?langs) WHERE {
  VALUES ?item { %s }
  ?item wdt:P50 ?author .
  OPTIONAL { ?author rdfs:label ?authorEn FILTER(LANG(?authorEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P31 ?type . OPTIONAL { ?type rdfs:label ?typeEn FILTER(LANG(?typeEn) = "en") } }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P407 ?lang . }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P577 ?date . }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv . FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?en . FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
} GROUP BY ?item

```

**6. Labels (sv, mul, en) of every author of an eligible work (run by <scratch>/author_labels.py, 200 per request)** (Wikidata: literary works with a Swedish author, their labels, authors (P50), language (P407) and sitelinks)

```
SELECT ?a ?sv ?mul ?en WHERE { VALUES ?a { %s }
  OPTIONAL { ?a rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?a rdfs:label ?mul FILTER(LANG(?mul) = "mul") }
  OPTIONAL { ?a rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") } }
```

**7. Swedish-language records of every eligible work (python3 <scratch>/libris_count.py; one search per work, all pages: start=1, 201, 401 …). The searches of the 60 selected works (first page):** (LIBRIS — the Swedish union catalogue (xsearch API))

**15. Exploration, not used for the selection: Swedish-language works by Swedish citizens (q1, first query below); notable works (P800) of Swedish writers (q3, second query below). The P5101 and q2 queries follow in queries 16 and 17.** (Wikidata: literary works with a Swedish author, their labels, authors (P50), language (P407) and sitelinks)

```
SELECT ?item ?sitelinks (SAMPLE(?sv) AS ?svLabel) (SAMPLE(?en) AS ?enLabel) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?author), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?authors) (MIN(YEAR(?date)) AS ?firstYear) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?type), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?types) WHERE {
  ?item wdt:P407 wd:Q9027 ;
        wdt:P50 ?author ;
        wikibase:sitelinks ?sitelinks .
  FILTER(?sitelinks >= 8)
  ?author wdt:P27 wd:Q34 .
  ?item wdt:P31 ?type .
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P577 ?date . }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv . FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?en . FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
}
GROUP BY ?item ?sitelinks
ORDER BY DESC(?sitelinks)

SELECT ?author ?authorLabel ?aLinks ?work ?workSv ?workEn ?wLinks (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?type), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?types) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?lang), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?langs) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?wa), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?workAuthors) WHERE {
  ?author wdt:P27 wd:Q34 ;
          wdt:P106 wd:Q36180 ;
          wdt:P800 ?work ;
          wikibase:sitelinks ?aLinks .
  FILTER(?aLinks >= 20)
  ?work wikibase:sitelinks ?wLinks .
  OPTIONAL { ?work wdt:P31 ?type . }
  OPTIONAL { ?work wdt:P407 ?lang . }
  OPTIONAL { ?work wdt:P50 ?wa . }
  OPTIONAL { ?author rdfs:label ?authorLabel . FILTER(LANG(?authorLabel) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?work rdfs:label ?workSv . FILTER(LANG(?workSv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?work rdfs:label ?workEn . FILTER(LANG(?workEn) = "en") }
}
GROUP BY ?author ?authorLabel ?aLinks ?work ?workSv ?workEn ?wLinks
ORDER BY DESC(?aLinks) DESC(?wLinks)

```

**17. Exploration (q2): works by any author with a Litteraturbanken ID and at least 6 sitelinks, in one query; timed out** (Wikidata: literary works with a Swedish author, their labels, authors (P50), language (P407) and sitelinks)

```
SELECT ?item ?sitelinks (SAMPLE(?sv) AS ?svLabel) (SAMPLE(?en) AS ?enLabel) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?author), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?authors) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?cit), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?citizenship) (MIN(YEAR(?date)) AS ?firstYear) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?type), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?types) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STRAFTER(STR(?lang), "entity/"); separator="|") AS ?langs) WHERE {
  {
    SELECT DISTINCT ?item ?sitelinks WHERE {
      ?author wdt:P5101 [] .
      ?item wdt:P50 ?author ;
            wikibase:sitelinks ?sitelinks .
      FILTER(?sitelinks >= 6)
    }
  }
  ?item wdt:P50 ?author .
  OPTIONAL { ?author wdt:P27 ?cit . }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P31 ?type . }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P407 ?lang . }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P577 ?date . }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv . FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?en . FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
}
GROUP BY ?item ?sitelinks
ORDER BY DESC(?sitelinks)

```

## Quality control

6 rounds, 44 findings: 36 fixed, 2 rejected after checking, 6 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (371 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Selection rule, sources, licences and machine checks: every card's Swedish title and author against Wikidata, LIBRIS and Swedish Wikipedia (and English Wikipedia where there is an article); every English title against LIBRIS and Open Library. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 60 cards, the candidate pool and ranking, the sources and the deck metadata.

All 60 cards agree across Wikidata, LIBRIS and the Wikipedia leads on the author, and every Swedish title is the title of Swedish LIBRIS records of the work. All 361 Wikidata checks pass. The findings are about the selection measure, Wikidata's English labels and the modelling of the two author partnerships; no Wikidata check was skipped because Wikidata disagreed with a better source.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| deck | A ranking by Wikimedia sitelinks alone (cap of three per author, at least 5 sitelinks) was dominated by recent crime fiction (three novels each by Stieg Larsson, David Lagercrantz, Henning Mankell, Sjöwall and Wahlöö and Camilla Läckberg) and left out Röda rummet, Hemsöborna, Pippi Långstrump (book item 23 sitelinks, below three other Lindgren books), Utvandrarna (3 sitelinks; the series item has 10) and Det går an. | The score combines sitelinks with the number of Swedish-language LIBRIS records (geometric mean), which measures publication in Sweden; method step 4. | fixed |
| deck | A ranking by LIBRIS count alone put Lagerlöf's En herrgårdssägen and Herr Arnes penningar above Nils Holgerssons underbara resa genom Sverige (55 records) so that the cap left Nils Holgersson out. | Resolved by the combined score (Nils Holgersson has 45 sitelinks and ranks first). | fixed |
| gosta-berlings-saga | Wikidata's English label "Gösta Berlings Saga" is the Swedish genitive form; English editions use "Gösta Berling's Saga" (LIBRIS records from 1898), "The Story of Gösta Berling" (LIBRIS and Open Library) and "The Saga of Gösta Berling" (LIBRIS, 2009). | English front "Gösta Berling's Saga", the English Wikipedia article title, attested by LIBRIS and Open Library; no English label check on this card. | fixed |
| stenhuggaren | Wikidata's English label "The Stone Cutter" matches no English edition; the HarperCollins translation (2010) is "The Stonecutter" (LIBRIS, English Wikipedia). | English front "The Stonecutter"; no English label check. | fixed |
| hundraaringen | The English Wikipedia title and Wikidata label "The Hundred-Year-Old Man Who Climbed Out the Window and Disappeared" match no LIBRIS or Open Library record exactly; the Wikidata alias "The 100-Year-Old Man Who Climbed Out the Window and Disappeared" matches both. | English front from the alias, checked as an English alias. | fixed |
| ronja-rovardotter | Two English titles are published: "Ronia, the Robber's Daughter" (LIBRIS records 1983, 1985, 2010) and "Ronja, the Robber's Daughter" (LIBRIS 2018, the English Wikipedia article title). | The rule takes the English Wikipedia title, which is attested; both are Wikidata English names. Superseded in rounds 1–2: the card now shows "Ronia, the Robber's Daughter", the title of most English editions. | no change needed |
| ondskan | English Wikipedia calls the novel "Evil" (also the Wikidata English label, and the title of the film), but no English-language edition by Guillou with that title was found in LIBRIS or Open Library. | English front is the Swedish title "Ondskan". | fixed |
| det-gar-an | No English label or article; an English translation was published as "Sara Videbeck" (1919, with The Chapel; LIBRIS), a title that is not a translation of "Det går an". Likewise Frithiofs saga has English editions as "Frithiof's Saga" (LIBRIS, e.g. 1839) and Markurells i Wadköping as "God's Orchid" (1924) and "The Markurells of Wadköping" (2016), titles that are neither a Wikidata English name nor an English Wikipedia title. | The rule keeps the Swedish title on the English side of these cards rather than choosing among titles by hand. Superseded in rounds 1–2: "The Markurells of Wadköping" differs from Wikidata's English label only by its article, so the claim above about it was wrong; the cards now show "Sara Videbeck", "Frithiof's Saga" and "The Markurells of Wadköping". | no change needed |
